name: Iowa veterans: County Veteran Service Officers for claims help
description: Free help with VA claims, appeals, pension and survivor benefits from the accredited County Veteran Service Officer in each of Iowa’s 99 county veterans affairs offices. County commissions of veteran affairs may also offer local emergency help. The Iowa Department of Veterans Affairs runs the Iowa Veterans Benefits Office at Camp Dodge.
next_step: Choose a county above for its veterans affairs office. Or call the Iowa Department of Veterans Affairs at 515-252-4698 or 800-838-4692.
constraints: Many rural offices keep limited hours; call ahead.

name: LifeLong Links and Iowa’s Area Agencies on Aging
organization: Iowa Department of Health and Human Services and the six Area Agencies on Aging
description: LifeLong Links is Iowa’s statewide aging and disability resource line; it connects older adults, people with disabilities and caregivers to their local Area Agency on Aging and long-term services. Military service is not required.
next_step: Call LifeLong Links at 866-468-7887, or choose a county above for its Area Agency on Aging.
constraints: Each program has its own eligibility and waitlist.

name: Medicare counseling (SHIIP) for Iowa
organization: Iowa Insurance Division, Senior Health Insurance Information Program (SHIIP)
description: Free, unbiased Medicare counseling from Iowa’s State Health Insurance Assistance Program, SHIIP, with trained volunteer counselors at local sites.
next_step: Call SHIIP at 800-351-4664 (TTY 800-735-2942) to reach a counselor near you. For Medicare itself, call 800-MEDICARE (800-633-4227).
constraints: Counselor availability is limited during open enrollment; call early.

name: Iowa Long-Term Care Ombudsman and dependent adult abuse reporting
organization: Iowa HHS: Office of the State Long-Term Care Ombudsman; Dependent Adult Abuse Program
description: Free, confidential advocacy for people living in nursing facilities, assisted living, residential care and elder group homes. Iowa HHS takes reports of abuse, neglect or exploitation of dependent adults living in the community, 24 hours a day.
next_step: Call the ombudsman at 866-236-1430. To report dependent adult abuse in the community, call 800-362-2178 (24/7). For abuse in a licensed facility, call the Department of Inspections, Appeals and Licensing at 877-686-0027. In an emergency, call 911.
constraints: The ombudsman acts with the resident’s permission and is not a licensing agency.

source_evidence.title: Iowa HHS: Office of the State Long-Term Care Ombudsman
source_evidence.scope: Toll-free 866-236-1430 and mailing address; read in full. Updated September 30, 2026.

source_evidence.title: Iowa HHS: Adult Protective Services
source_evidence.scope: Report dependent adult abuse at 1-800-362-2178, 24/7; facility abuse 1-877-686-0027; search excerpt.

name: Free legal help for older Iowans
organization: Iowa Legal Aid, Legal Hotline for Older Iowans
description: The Legal Hotline for Older Iowans gives free civil legal help to Iowans 60 and older. Iowa Legal Aid helps low-income Iowans of any age.
next_step: Age 60 and older: call the Legal Hotline for Older Iowans at 800-992-8161 (515-282-8161 in Des Moines). Under 60: Iowa Legal Aid, 800-532-1503.
constraints: The hotline handles civil matters only.

name: VA health care systems serving Iowa
description: Iowa veterans are served by the VA Central Iowa Health Care System (Des Moines VA Medical Center, 3600 30th Street; 515-699-5999, toll-free 800-294-8387) and the Iowa City VA Health Care System (601 Highway 6 West; 319-338-0581, toll-free 800-637-0128). Some western and northwestern counties are closer to VA systems in Omaha and Sioux Falls.
next_step: Call the system nearest you, or use VA’s facility locator with your ZIP code. Not enrolled yet? Ask your county veterans affairs office for help applying.
constraints: Which system serves you depends on where you live; VA’s locator shows the right clinic.

name: Access 2 Independence (A2I)
description: A Center for Independent Living: disability-led help with daily living skills, peer support, advocacy, assistive technology referrals and moving from a nursing home back to the community. Any age and any disability; military service is not required.
next_step: Call with your county and goals. Ask about intake, home access, independent living skills or help leaving a facility.
constraints: A Center for Independent Living is a community support organization, not a residential care facility. Services depend on assessment and availability.
Main office: 1556 South First Avenue, Suite B, Iowa City. Toll-free: 866-338-4544. Cedar Rapids office: 601 2nd Ave SE.
